answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent network authenticates nodes via near-field soil induction. As mobile units wander through a grove, each pulses current through a copper probe near a cedar trunk to sample localized eddy-current decay. Forging identities requires coupling with distinct physical terrain, imposing hardware fabrication and deployment costs on an adversary per node. However, fluctuating ground moisture distorts conductivity baselines, occasionally causing false rejections.
